name: Kamailio
what_it_is: Kamailio is an industrial-strength, open-source SIP server (RFC 3261) for real-time communications including IP telephony, instant messaging, and presence at scale. It runs as a core process plus pluggable modules, capable of serving millions of users and acting as registrar, proxy, SBC, IMS server, PSTN gateway guard, or presence server.
components: Modular plugin architecture (modules loaded at startup via kamailio.cfg)
EVAPI interface (event API for third-party integration)
DB abstraction layer (supports MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQLite, Redis, etc.)
measurement: Syslog-based logging with configurable log levels
SIP trace / Homer integration via sipcapture module
configuration: Primary config file: kamailio.cfg (routing script DSL)
Module parameters set via modparam() directives in kamailio.cfg
TLS configured via tls.cfg or inline modparams
Listen addresses/ports defined with listen= directives
Worker processes controlled with children= directive
constraints: No built-in fault injection primitives — failure simulation requires external tooling or custom routing script logic
No native docker-compose file in the official repository — containerized deployments rely on community images (e.g., kamailio/kamailio on Docker Hub)
Configuration language is a custom DSL (kamailio.cfg routing script); not YAML/JSON — steep learning curve for first-time operators
Shared-memory architecture limits horizontal scaling to multiple independent nodes; no native clustering state sync without external DB
notable_absences: No docker-compose.yml in the official kamailio/kamailio repository (checked master and main branches)
No built-in fault injection or chaos engineering features
No built-in metrics endpoint in Prometheus format (requires third-party exporter)
No GUI or web dashboard included
